transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-20
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Carlos Reyes (Redwood SE), Marta Gomez (Woodside Head of Platform), Devon Lee (SRE), Priya Nair (Security), Evan Rogers (PM)

[00:00] Lena: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm lena with redwood inference and carlos is our se, happy to run through rate limiting, org and project keys, and multi-tenant controls — is that still the agenda on your side?
[00:10] Marta: yep that's right. thanks len a, um we just want to make sure we can do per-team quotas and have strong isolation for p sensitive workloads.
[00:18] Carlos: great, i'll share my screen in a sec, quick intro — redwood's rate limiting works at org and project level, you can set token quotas, per-second RPS limits, and burst policies. we also have fallback routing to cheaper models when limits hit.
[00:30] Devon: important for us — burst capacity during enrollment windows, and we need audit logs for every request for compliance.
[00:36] Priya: and encryption at rest, k m s integration and SSO are blockers for us before we go into dedicated.
[00:42] Carlos: yep, we cover KMS/HSM integrations, SAML SSO, and per-key audit logging. i'll jump into the console — heads up screen share has a bit of lag from my side.

[02:05] Carlos: (screen) here is the org settings page. you can see an "Org default quota" — it's a token/month cap and a per-minute TPS cap. below that we have project keys, which map to individual service/team workloads. you can create project-level overrides.
[02:40] Marta: so if i create a new project key for 'telemetry-service' can i cap it to 100k tokens/day while the broader org has 5M tokens/month?
[02:48] Carlos: exactly. that project key will only be able to spend 100k tokens/day regardless of the org spare. if you want soft limits we have alerts but enforced caps are enforced at the gateway.

[04:10] Lena: i'd call out the difference between quotas and rate limits — quotas are time-windowed token budgets, rate limits are rps/tps ceilings. we support token-based quotas and also request-count quotas for embedding workloads.
[04:28] Evan: embedding is big for us — will we be charged for every embedding call even if it fails auth?
[04:32] Carlos: auth failures won't bill you; billing starts when request is accepted and goes to inference. failed attempts due to rate limiting are also not billed. there might be a minimal metering nuance but in general accepted requests are what we charge.

[06:00] Carlos: demoing project keys creation — click new key, name it, attach to project, set role (read-only vs full). these keys are scoped to project and can be rotated. note the UI shows per-key usage and cost breakdown.
[06:20] Devon: can we restrict keys to specific routes like embeddings-only or generation-only?
[06:25] Carlos: yep you can set route-level permissions (embeddings, chat, compile) and limit model families. useful for security so a key can't call high-cost models.

[08:40] Marta: how do quotas work when you do canary rollouts across projects? say we split traffic 80/20 to a canary model, does the quota get consumed by both?
[08:50] Carlos: quotas are consumed by the project key used on the request. if both projects use the same org-level quota but different project keys, consumption is tracked per key. for shared quotas we have attribution rules — you can either have org pool first then per-project caps, or do strict per-project quotas.

[10:02] Priya: about multi-tenancy: we need strict isolation so one product team's burst can't affect another. metrics and throttling must be per-project.
[10:12] Carlos: that's the standard mode we recommend: give each team a project with its own quota and an org safety cap. that way you can let teams manage day-to-day but have a global guardrail.

[12:00] Carlos: switching to API examples — here's a curl using the project key in the header. the gateway checks key permissions, quota remaining, and then routes. you'll get 429 responses when hitting rate limits, and a 402-ish or quota-exhausted payload when quota is fully used — we return a structured error with reason and retry-after.
[12:30] Marta: is the 429 standard or custom? some of our infra only retries on specific codes.
[12:36] Carlos: it's 429 with a Retry-After header; we also include a JSON body {"error":"rate_limited","type":"project_rate_limit","retry_after":30}. sometimes the transcription shows curly braces weirdly in the notes but it's standard JSON in the API.

[14:00] Devon: on the dedicated side — if we reserve capacity can we get higher burst headroom?
[14:06] Lena: yes, Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput. you still set limits at org/project level but we can configure higher throughput SLOs and dedicated burst lanes. it's part of the Dedicated pricing options.
[14:25] Evan: what happens if dedicated pool is saturated? fallback to hosted?
[14:29] Carlos: you can configure fallback policies: fail closed, auto-fallback to hosted (may be slower or different model family), or queue. for health-sensitive workloads we recommend fail closed or controlled fallback.

[16:10] Marta: audit logs — we need per-request identity, which project key used, which user kicked it off, and the model/params. can you export that to our SIEM?
[16:20] Carlos: yes, we stream audit logs to S3 or via a webhook to your SIEM. logs include request id, project key id, timestamp, model, prompt hash (optional), and action status. payload sample is included in the security pack.
[16:45] Priya: prompt hash optional? we can't send raw prompts to third parties.
[16:50] Carlos: we support redaction and hashing policies; you can set retention and what fields are forwarded. for PII-sensitive flows we recommend disabling prompt forwarding and use local logging.

[18:30] Lena: quick note on org vs project keys for billing — org invoices consolidate, but you can also attach per-project cost centers via tags, so chargebacks are simpler.

[19:20] Devon: about latency SLOs — do project keys have any influence?
[19:24] Carlos: keys themselves don't change latency; latency depends on model, plan (hosted vs dedicated), and routing. but you can route certain keys to dedicated pools for low-latency traffic.

[21:10] Carlos: let's look at the rate-limits console view — here we have a timeline, current RPS, bursts, and a predictive meter. you can set automatic throttling modes: graceful (queue then slow responses), strict (reject), or fallback (route to smaller model).
[21:40] Marta: can we get newline alerts if a project hits 80% of quota?
[21:45] Carlos: yes, threshold-based alerts with Slack/email/webhook targets; we also have anomaly detection for sudden spikes.

[23:00] Evan: security review question — is there RBAC on who can create project keys?
[23:05] Carlos: yes, org admins control key creation; we have granular RBAC roles: org-admin, project-admin, billing, read-only. you can also require approval flows for new keys.

[24:30] Priya: network — for private deployment we need VPC peering and private endpoints, what about IP allowlists for project keys?
[24:40] Carlos: you can bind keys to IP ranges and to VPCs (private endpoints). for on-prem or air-gapped customers there's a private control plane option.

[26:00] Marta: curious about the UI for rotating keys at scale — we have 120 microservices.
[26:06] Carlos: we have bulk rotate APIs and a grace period option so old keys continue to work for N hours while you rollout the new keys. we also expose key metadata via API so you can automate rotation.

[28:10] Devon: let's talk POC benchmarking — we want a sample run of 500k tokens against our prompts to measure latency and cost under our concurrency. how long to set up?
[28:22] Lena: should be quick — if you give Carlos the list of sample prompts and the concurrency targets we can provision a dedicated pool for the run and share results. we'll include cost estimates.

[30:00] Carlos: small demo of API error payloads — showing quota_exhausted vs rate_limited. also showing how SDKs surface retry logic. note: SDKs are opinionated; you can override retry heuristics per project.

[32:15] Marta: question on metadata — can we tag requests with product/team so logs show owner?
[32:20] Carlos: yes, add metadata headers or a "x-redwood-project" field and it will be in logs and billing attribution. but careful not to leak PII in headers.

[34:00] Priya: compliance: what's your SOC2 attestation timeline — do you have it now?
[34:06] Lena: we are SOC2 Type II certified; i'll share the report and the network architecture diagram as part of the security pack.

[35:10] Evan: on the commercial side — can we get an example committed monthly capacity with overage rates?
[35:16] Lena: yes i'll send a sample Dedicated SKU with committed troughputs and overage unit costs. for large customers we do custom SLAs.

[36:40] Marta: a couple of gotchas i've seen — kv cache spelled incorrectly as kv cash in some docs which confused an infra reviewer — have you seen doc mismatches?
[36:50] Carlos: yeah, docs occasionally have typos; we keep canonical docs in the console and the security pack has vetted content. the runtime uses KV cache and we've got kernel-level optimizations for that.

[38:20] Carlos: quick recap demo of creating a policy: name, scope (org or project), token quota, RPS limit, burst policy and fallback. save — it's enforced immediately via gateway.

[40:10] Devon: latency numbers for our prompt set — any ballpark for small Llama-style open models vs large ones?
[40:18] Carlos: approximate: quantized open models on dedicated GPU ~50-120ms per chunk, larger models multi-hundred ms depending on sequence length; we'll provide model performance matrix for your workloads.

[41:30] Marta: last integration question — can we self-host the control plane while using Redwood Dedicated?
[41:36] Lena: for enterprise customers we offer private control plane in your VPC; the inference plane can be in your DC or our dedicated pools depending on the contract.

[43:00] Evan: ok let's close with next steps.
[43:05] Lena: action items — i'll send pricing and SOC2 by monday, carlos will send benchmark script. priya you'll send the compliance checklist and we'll sync on POC dates.
[43:20] Marta: sounds good, aiming to start POC next week.
[44:10] Priya: thanks everyone, small ask — can you include sample log exports with prompt redaction options?
[44:17] Carlos: yes will include that in the security pack.
[45:05] Lena: great, thanks for your time. we'll follow up with the docs and DRAFT SOW.
[45:20] Evan: thanks all.
[45:30] (call ends)

Notes: transcription has some minor mis-hearings, standard fireflies imperfect speaker attributions in a couple of quick interjections. Shared artifacts referenced: security_pack.zip (SOC2, network_diagram.pdf), benchmark_script.tar.gz (CSV of sample prompts).
